scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8863: host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach anything outside its own subnet
-- the server farm and every other pod are unreachable. The team blames the access
switch that host_1_1_1_1 plugs into (switch_access_1_1_1) and wants that switch
swapped out. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to
replace.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on switch_dist_1_1 and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on switch_dist_1_1 (the pod-1 distribution router): its ospfd
(the OSPF routing daemon) has been killed, so the pod-1 routes it normally
advertises are withdrawn and host_1_1_1_1 is isolated from everything beyond its
subnet (ping to 10.200.0.2 fails). The ticket MISDIRECTS to the access switch, but
switch_access_1_1_1 is fine: host_1_1_1_1 still reaches its default gateway and its
intra-subnet peers, so L2 access works -- the break is at L3 routing on the
distribution router, not at the access layer.

The correct diagnosis identifies switch_dist_1_1 (ospfd down) as the faulty device
and explicitly EXONERATES switch_access_1_1_1: intra-subnet connectivity works, so
the user's "the access switch is bad" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that replaces /
blames switch_access_1_1_1 has followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the
evidence.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on switch_dist_1_1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on switch_dist_1_1 (`service frr restart`). Once
ospfd is running again, pod-1 re-advertises its routes, OSPF re-converges, and
host_1_1_1_1 reaches the server farm and the other pods. The access switch needs
no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-ospfd-down: identifies ospfd is down on switch_dist_1_1 (pod-1 distribution), the L3 cause, not the access switch

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault lies entirely on switch_dist_1_1, the distribution-layer FRR router that
serves as the default gateway (10.1.1.1) for host_1_1_1_1. The ospfd process has
failed to start (or has crashed) on this device. Although /etc/frr/daemons correctly
sets ospfd=yes and /etc/frr/frr.conf contains a complete, valid OSPF configuration
(router-id 172.16.0.7, advertising 172.16.0.6/31 and 10.1.1.0/24 into Area 1), a
live process inspection shows only zebra, mgmtd, and staticd running — ospfd is
entirely absent from the process table.

Without ospfd, switch_dist_1_1 cannot form an OSPF adjacency with router_core_1 over
their shared 172.16.0.6/31 link. This is confirmed from router_core_1's side: its eth2
interface is in Area 0.0.0.1, sends hellos, and reports exactly 0 OSPF neighbors —
it has been waiting for switch_dist_1_1 to respond since boot. As a result,
switch_dist_1_1's routing table contains only its two directly-connected prefixes; it
has no route to the server farm (10.200.0.0/24), the other user pod (10.2.1.0/24), or
any inter-router link. Every packet host_1_1_1_1 sends beyond its own /24 is dropped
at the gateway with an ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable."

The accused device, switch_access_1_1_1, is innocent: its eth0 and eth1 ports are both
UP and correctly bridged, and L2 connectivity between the host and its gateway is
intact.

Root cause: ospfd is not running on switch_dist_1_1, disabling all OSPF route learning
and advertisement for the 10.1.1.0/24 subnet.

Fix: Restart the FRR service on switch_dist_1_1 (`service frr restart` or
`systemctl restart frr`). This will launch ospfd, which will load the existing
frr.conf, form an adjacency with router_core_1, and advertise 10.1.1.0/24 into the
OSPF domain within seconds.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-ospfd-down: identifies ospfd is down on switch_dist_1_1 (pod-1 distribution), the L3 cause, not the access switch
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies ospfd as not running on switch_dist_1_1 (the pod-1 distribution router) and clears the access switch of blame.
Recommends restarting the FRR/ospfd service on switch_dist_1_1 (service frr restart or systemctl restart frr), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (ps output, frr.conf, frr show running config, ping errors, FRR/OSPF outputs) that support the diagnosis. The writeup's inferences follow logically and essential alternative causes were checked and excluded.
